_note: SF Symbol name -> cross-platform icon resolution. THE #1 .dsx portability seam: icon=/systemImage=/tabIcon=/actionIcon= (and the snapshot dialect's symbol=) name SF Symbols, which exist only on Apple platforms (and may not be redistributed). iOS renders the SF name directly (the fast path); every other runtime resolves it HERE. Per entry: `material` = the Material Symbols name (Apache-2.0, google/material-design-icons), `codepoint` = that glyph's hex codepoint in the Material Symbols font (the PUA cmap slot - render the char at this codepoint with the bundled font), `fallback` = a plain unicode/text stand-in for when no icon font is available (best-effort; a renderer with neither font nor fallback draws its placeholder). Fail-open: an SF name not in this table renders the consumer's placeholder, never an error. Keyed by the SF name because the .dsx corpus is SF-named (StackReference.md: the icon attribute is a semantic token resolved by the same name on every platform - never a per-platform id). COVERAGE: every distinct icon=/symbol= literal in the shipped .dsx corpus (ClosedSource/DSX/Modules, incl. ternary/default-expression literals) + the StackReference.md defaults (EmptyState `tray`, the tab examples). Adding an icon to markup? Add its row here in the same change - Android consumes this file as a packaged :render asset (see OpenSource/Engine/Android/render/build.gradle.kts copySfMapJson; ONE file, never forked).
_fill_axis: SF `.fill` variants map to the SAME material name as their outline sibling: Material Symbols express fill as a variable-font FILL axis, and the bundled Android subset is instanced at the default FILL=0 (outline) look. A filled-vs-outline pair that must stay visually distinct (selection states) maps to two DIFFERENT material glyphs instead - see circle -> radio_button_unchecked vs circle.fill -> fiber_manual_record.
_web_axis: `web` = the row's 24x24 SVG path `d` for renderers that have neither the Material Symbols font nor SF Symbols - the browsers. AXIS v2 (owner-directed 2026-08-23): the paths are FILL paths taken from Boxicons (MIT - license text at BOXICONS-LICENSE beside this file), drawn fill: currentColor, stroke: none (elements.ts iconSvg). iOS keeps drawing the SF name directly and Android keeps the Material codepoint - this axis is the web tier only. Render ladder unchanged: `web` path -> `fallback` unicode text -> the consumer's placeholder, fail-open.
_subset_provenance: The bundled Android asset (OpenSource/Engine/Android/render/src/main/assets/despia/icons/MaterialSymbolsOutlined-subset.ttf) is generated FROM google/material-design-icons variablefont/MaterialSymbolsOutlined[FILL,GRAD,opsz,wght].ttf (name-table Version 2.963, Apache-2.0) BY: fontTools varLib.instancer at the default axes (wght=400 FILL=0 GRAD=0 opsz=24) then pyftsubset --unicodes=<every `codepoint` in this file>. Regenerate the subset in the SAME change as any row addition; :render's FontSubsetTest fails the build when a row's codepoint is missing from the shipped cmap.
_license: Material Symbols (google/material-design-icons) is Apache License 2.0 - redistribution of the font subset + this name/codepoint table is permitted with attribution; the license text ships next to the bundled font (OpenSource/Engine/Android/render/src/main/assets/despia/icons/). The `web` axis paths are extracted from Boxicons 2.1.4 (github.com/atisawd/boxicons; MIT, elected from its CC-BY-4.0 OR OFL-1.1 OR MIT tri-license) - path data only, no fonts/css/js; the MIT text is BOXICONS-LICENSE beside this file.
_web_extra_note: Names the WEB renderer draws that are not (yet) rows of `icons` above. They are authored by the in-repo web demos/previews (the device-agnostic Live Activity + Watch previews, the settings and bookmark chrome), so web must draw them; they are NOT in `icons` because a row there also pins a Material Symbols codepoint that must exist in the bundled Android subset font (OpenSource/Engine/Android/render FontSubsetTest), and regenerating that subset is a separate, Android-owned change. Promoting one is exactly that: pick its material name, regenerate the subset font, move the row up. Until then this section is the explicit, documented divergence - web-only coverage, recorded in the shared table rather than forked into the web package. Shape: SF name -> the same 24x24 stroke path `d` as an `icons` row's `web` field. These rows carry NO codepoint by construction. TWO POPULATIONS live here: the demo/preview names above (plain SF spellings, promotable), and the `dsx.` prefixed STUDIO GLYPHS described in _studio_glyph_note.
_studio_glyph_note: The `dsx.` prefixed rows of web_extra are the Despia Studio's own glyph vocabulary - one icon per node the visual editors can draw (every JSE operator, every higher-order container, every named method, every statement kind). They carry the prefix BECAUSE THEY ARE NOT SF SYMBOLS and never will be: iOS cannot draw `dsx.multiply`, and the prefix says so at a glance rather than hiding a Studio name among the shipping ones. ClosedSource/DSX/Modules/Custom/Editor has no swift/ and no kotlin/ lane - it is a hosted web surface - so these names never reach Image(systemName:) or the Material subset font, and paying the Android font tax for them would buy nothing. Two sources: most are Boxicons 2.1.4 fill paths like every other row of this tier (MIT, BOXICONS-LICENSE beside this file); the ~15 pure OPERATOR symbols (dsx.multiply, dsx.divide, dsx.percent, dsx.equal, dsx.notequal, dsx.lessthan, dsx.greaterthan, dsx.atmost, dsx.atleast, dsx.caret, dsx.pipe, dsx.not, dsx.power, dsx.and, dsx.or) are drawn here on the same 24x24, 2px-bar grid, because no icon set ships a division sign. The gate that keeps a Studio glyph honest is OpenSource/Web/packages/cli/test/exprflow.test.ts + packages/dom/test/icons.test.ts: every name either editor emits must resolve in this file.
